audit_findings.title: The anchor may capitalize a one-time leadership-transition penalty into perpetuity
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.172 million after tax ($6.640 million cost less $0.468 million disclosed tax benefit), equal to 82.3% of the $7.5 million anchor; computed value effect approximately $2.43-$4.43 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The cash transition bonuses reduce FY2025 owner earnings and, if left in the anchor, are projected through the explicit period and terminal value as though recurring.
audit_findings.evidence: Selling, general, and administrative expenses increased $9.9 million primarily due to $6.6 million in bonuses related to our executive leadership transition, and $3.0 million in stock compensation related to new executive leadership compensation arrangements.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed expense and associated tax benefit are demonstrated, and the company labels the compensation nonrecurring. It is not yet demonstrated that the $7.5 million anchor failed to normalize it or that every dollar was genuinely nonrecurring. A verified adjustment would nearly double the anchor and materially change the intrinsic-value range, although the resulting approximate $5.51-$9.97 per-share range would remain below the $21.53 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $7.5 million anchor line by line; verify the cash payment, contractual purpose, absence of replacement compensation, and actual $0.468 million tax benefit; then rerun all scenarios adding back only the verified after-tax cash transition cost while retaining stock compensation.

audit_findings.title: Completed headquarters renovations may be misclassified as recurring maintenance capital expenditure
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2025 total cash capital expenditures were $10.706 million versus the $7.5 million anchor, including $2.8 million of capitalized internal-use software costs
audit_findings.mechanism: If project-related renovation spending was included in the maintenance-capex deduction, it depresses FY2025 owner earnings and every forecast and terminal-value period based on that anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Depreciation, amortization and impairment expenses increased in 2025 compared to the 2024 period due to the completion of our headquarters building renovations in June 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Completion of the headquarters renovation and the total capital-expenditure amount are demonstrated, but the filing does not identify how much FY2025 cash spending related to that completed project. Because total capex exceeded the anchor and the potentially nonrecurring component is unresolved, the issue is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2025 fixed-asset and cash-capex ledgers by project; reconcile them to the $10.706 million cash-flow amount and accounts-payable movements; rerun the valuation excluding only verified headquarters-project spending while retaining maintenance, equipment replacement, and recurring software-development investment.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest may escape an equity-level owner-earnings calculation
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.551 million for FY2025, equal to 7.3% of the $7.5 million anchor; maximum dollar-for-dollar computed value effect approximately $0.22-$0.40 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized cash interest could be omitted from current interest expense and then neutralized by a depreciation add-back unless it is captured once in operating cash flow or the capital-expenditure deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest capitalized for 2025, 2024, and 2023 was $551,000, $1.0 million, and $566,000, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Capitalization of $0.551 million is demonstrated, but omission from owner earnings is only a possibility until the calculation is traced. Even assuming the entire amount escaped the calculation and should reduce the anchor dollar for dollar, the scenario values would fall by only about $0.22-$0.40 per share and remain far below the $21.53 market price; the valuation conclusion would not change.
audit_findings.action: Trace capitalized interest through cash from operations, capital expenditures, and the depreciation add-back to confirm it is deducted exactly once; correct the owner-earnings series if it is missing.

audit_findings.title: An uncertain-tax liability may be an unbridged claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.4 million gross liability at both December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026; maximum bridge effect approximately $0.10 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpaid cash settlement not already reflected in owner earnings would be a claim deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The liability for gross unrecognized tax benefits related to uncertain tax positions was $2.4 million as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The gross liability is demonstrated, but a separate valuation omission is not: the expected settlement amount, timing, and overlap with cash taxes remain unresolved. Even deducting the entire $2.4 million immediately would reduce equity value by only about $0.10 per share, or 1.9%-3.4% of the stated scenario equity values, without changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 uncertain-tax-position roll-forward to cash taxes and projected owner earnings; deduct only the expected remaining cash settlement not already captured.

audit_findings.title: Stakes_net of zero may omit disclosed strategic equity investments
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the investments are included within the $2.664 million June 2026 other-noncurrent-assets balance, but their individual carrying and realizable values are not disclosed
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonoperating investments whose earnings are excluded from owner earnings should be added separately in stakes_net at realizable value, without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: We make equity investments to promote business and strategic objectives.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence and accounting policy for equity investments are demonstrated, while omission of material value is not. Their carrying amount, ownership, and realizable value cannot be isolated from the filed record; cost-method carrying values can also differ from realizable value. The issue may affect the bridge, but the record cannot establish its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain an investment-by-investment schedule showing issuer, ownership, carrying cost, observable transactions, impairment analysis, and realizable value; determine whether each investment is operating or nonoperating and rerun the bridge for verified nonoperating value.

audit_findings.title: All cash was added despite an apparent operating-liquidity requirement
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.327 million maximum disputed cash addition, equal to approximately $0.14 per share and 2.6%-4.7% of stated scenario equity values
audit_findings.mechanism: Only cash exceeding operating and contractual liquidity requirements belongs in the equity bridge as a distributable nonoperating asset.
audit_findings.evidence: We had a working capital deficit of $16.4 million and $16.3 million on December 31, 2025, and December 31, 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The $3.327 million cash balance and $12.2 million June 2026 working-capital deficit are demonstrated, but the required operating reserve is not. Even if none of the cash were surplus, removing the full balance would lower value by only about $0.14 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion. Deferred revenue also makes the headline working-capital deficit an incomplete measure of required cash.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a minimum-liquidity analysis covering payroll, taxes, deferred-revenue service costs, lease and debt payments, covenant headroom, and billing seasonality; replace the bridge addition with only the demonstrably surplus amount.
